title: Ben Payne Jazzland, the Pompey Room and the Gillis Theatre explosion
summary: After the Eblon he played a Twelfth Street club, the Pompey Room and the Gillis Theatre, and describes escaping an explosion there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And I left there. I played -- it was 12th Street then, they played at 12th Street in the nightclub called Ben Payne Jazzland, upstairs you know. We had a woman bouncer, you know, she weighed about 200. If a guy get tough in there man, you know, she'd take him and throw him down the steps. And from there let's see, I went to -- I'm trying to figure where did I go to after I left.
Yeah, Pompey Room downtown. And I stayed there for quite a while.
Would that be up into the late twenties?
Yes, in the late twenties. I went down there and they had an explosion at the theatre there then.
Oh, that's when you went to the Gillis Theatre.
What year was that, the late twenties or early thirties?
The twenties. Gillis -- yes, it seems to me I read about that. What happened there any way?

Well, any way they had a little hamburger joint right around the stand, right around the corner there, and the piano player and I, [Harris Wanigan,] we went around to this little hamburger joint. We started around there, as soon as we got into the lobby this explosion went off, man. Well, what happened, it was kind of misty rain that day -- that night, I mean, and I thought I was running up fast, you know, and I fell man, on the street with all that water, you know. You understand what I mean. Somebody said, I don't know who it was, oh, Baby's dead. And you talk about a guy scrambling man, I was -- I had mud all over me. So I came out of that all right. We stayed there for a long time.
You had a long stay at the Gillis. Well, of course you didn't go back to the Gillis Theatre.
